title: data labeling guidelines + samples (scratchpad)
body:
Notes / scratchpad - Data labeling cleanup + edge cases

Context:
- Working through noisy labels discovered in the customer chat dataset (prod ingestion, December 2024) - high false-positive rate on intent classification and inconsistent toxicity flags.
- Goal: produce minimal, actionable cleanup guidelines + a small set of canonical examples for the labeling UI and QA checks.

High-level goals:
1) Reduce ambiguity for annotators so inter-annotator agreement (IAA) improves from ~0.62 to >=0.8 on the dev seed.
2) Define explicit rules for common edge cases (sarcasm, quoted text, code snippets, bot messages).
3) Create a staging test set (200-400 samples) with canonical labels and short rationales we can use for retraining / calibration.

Quick rules (working list) - keep concise in UI cheat-sheet:
- Single best label only. If >1 label seems plausible, select the most explicit intent stated by the user. If implicit intent only, mark as "other/unsure" and flag.
- Toxicity: annotate for target-directed abuse. General profanity without a clear target = NOT toxicity (mark "not_toxic"). If profanity used sarcastically or quoting, include context note (see examples).
- Quote handling: If text contains quoted content from a third party (e.g., "they said '...'."), label the annotator-viewable content, not the quoted source, unless the speaker is the author and expresses the content.
- Code blocks/snippets: extract whether the message contains code. For intent classification, code-only messages -> label as "intent:technical/code". Comments embedded in code should follow the code-rule.
- Bot/system messages: messages that are machine-generated (system markers, e.g., "Assistant:" prefix) should be skipped for intent labels and annotated as "system_generated" in metadata.
- Unclear language / non-English: mark language tag and set label to "other/needs-review". We do not force guesswork.

Edge cases with examples (annotator cheat-sheet) - include these in UI tooltips:
1) Sarcasm / ironic compliment
- Text: "Great, another unpaid feature - just what I needed."
- Guidance: intent = intent:complaint (NOT praise). Toxicity = not_toxic (unless target present). Rationale: sarcasm expresses dissatisfaction.

2) Quoted profanity from a reported user
- Text: "He called me a 'dumb idiot'"
- Guidance: label toxicity only if the speaker endorses the content (e.g., "I called him a dumb idiot"). If quoting what someone else said about you, mark as "reported_abuse" metadata and toxicity=not_toxic unless the author repeats/endorses.

3) Multi-intent messages
- Text: "Can I upgrade my plan? Also my billing page is broken."
- Guidance: pick the dominant intent by order-of-ask (upgrade) OR if equal, mark as "multi_intent" and flag for multi-label QA pipeline. For now, prefer first explicit actionable request.

4) Code + natural language question
- Text: 
function foo() { return null; }
Why does this throw?
- Guidance: intent=intent:tech-support, tag contains_code=true. Annotator should capture technical intent and add code flag.

5) Short single-word messages
- Text: "Thanks" / "Ok" / "Nope"
- Guidance: classify as acknowledgment/negation/other based on lexicon; if too ambiguous -> "other/needs-review".

Labeling conventions (canonical):
- Use label ids: intent:purchase | intent:billing | intent:tech-support | intent:complaint | intent:other
- Toxicity: toxic | not_toxic | reported_abuse
- Additional flags: contains_code | system_generated | multi_intent | non_english | needs_review
- Rationale field: short free-text (1-2 sentences) when label != majority expectation (helps model interpret). Keep optional but encouraged for flagged samples.

Sampling plan for staging set:
- 200 samples: 40 typical purchase/billing/support each + 40 edge-case mixes (sarcasm, quotes, code, multi-intent).
- Ensure each sample has: raw_text, normalized_text (lowercase, strip non-sentential noise), label(s), flags, annotator_rationale.

Normalization / preprocessing notes (for labelers + pipeline):
- Strip agent name prefixes ("Assistant: ") before labeling (unless it's central to content).
- Normalize whitespace, convert unicode smart-quotes to ascii equivalents for UI display only (keep raw in data).
- Preserve punctuation relevant to meaning ("?", "!").

Quality control / acceptance criteria:
- IAA (Cohen's kappa) target >= 0.8 on dev seed.
- For flagged/needs-review samples, agreement threshold lowers to 0.6 but must have annotator rationale.
- Any label flip after 2 annotator disagreements -> escalate to lead reviewer (Asha).

Operational TODOs (next actions):
- [ ] Create initial 200-sample staging set (Maya) - sample pull, normalize, seed with 3 annotators each. (Due: 2025-02-09)
- [ ] Write UI tooltip copy for the top 10 rules and add "flag for review" quick-action (Asha)
- [ ] Add multi_intent flow to QA pipeline and small training signal to model reweighting (Samir)
- [ ] Draft confluence page / one-pager summarizing official rules and examples (Maya -> link to PR)

Notes to self:
- Keep examples short in UI; annotators lose focus with long multi-paragraph contexts. For long conversations, include a trimmed "relevant excerpt" field.
- We should log examples where model predictions diverge strongly from canonical labels and create a periodic "regression set".

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How to handle sarcasm that uses emoji? (Propose: treat emoji as amplifiers; include in rationale)
- Should we allow multi-label in the product long-term? (Tradeoff: annotation cost vs expressivity)

References / links, quick:
- Jira ticket for noisy labels: ML-2345
- Confluence draft: Data Labeling Guidelines Draft
- Dataset PR: github.com/redwood-inference/dataset/pull/98

End scratchpad - will tidy into a one-pager once staging set exists.

-- Maya
